text:
Condition: Urticaria (Hives)
Section: Symptoms
Subsection: Primary Manifestations

Primary Symptoms:
- Raised, itchy welts or wheals on the skin
- Wheals may be red, pink, or skin-colored
- Intense itching, burning, or stinging sensation
- Welts may appear and disappear rapidly
- Angioedema: deeper tissue swelling, often around eyes and lips

Onset Characteristics: Hives typically appear suddenly and can appear and disappear within minutes to hours. Lesions are highly pruritic and can be extremely uncomfortable.

Distribution Patterns: Can appear anywhere on the body, commonly on face, neck, torso, and extremities. In acute urticaria, welts typically resolve within 24 hours.

Severity Spectrum: Ranges from mild localized welts to severe widespread urticaria with associated systemic symptoms including fever and malaise in cases with underlying infection or severe allergic reaction.

Source: Clinical Medical Reference
